findings.title: Investigation grep scope leak: CWD vs repo-path
findings.detail: autodev investigate runs its grep from process CWD (the main autodev repo at /Users/macworkers/autodev) rather than from --repo-path. Evidence in the case file shows hits from autodev's own .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mypyc/ and tests/unit/test_edge_case_hunter.py — none from the brownfield target file src/widgetlib/calculator.py. This means investigation evidence is polluted with irrelevant files when the CLI is invoked from a different directory.

findings.title: Mock executor declares ghost changed_files that don't exist on disk
findings.detail: Each BUG-T* task's mock execution records changed_files=['.dev-factory/mock/codex_BUG-T*-*.txt'] but .dev-factory/mock/ directory is never created. The paths are phantom entries in the milestone_MBUG-1_results.json. Any downstream process that reads changed_files and tries to access them would get FileNotFoundError.

findings.title: Investigation produces no project-file code evidence
findings.detail: With evidence_count=5, all hits are from the wrong repository (CWD leak). The case file's Hypotheses section contains only the user-supplied description, not code-derived evidence. For a real brownfield scenario, this means investigate does not currently provide actionable code-level evidence; it's essentially a hypothesis recorder rather than a code explorer.
